newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Barley Board cuts feed barley price.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Barley Board cuts feed barley price.

text.p: The Australian Barley Board said on Monday it had revised its 1996/97 gross pool return estimates, with malting barley holding firm at A$210 a tonne, but the feed pool revised downward A$10 to A$147 per tonne.

In a statement, the ABB said malting barley had been under pressure from large world production and subsidy activity from the European Union, but weather in Canada had cast doubts about how much malting barley would be available there.
"It is bad luck for the Canadians, but our malting barley growers will benefit from a tightening in world supply," ABB general manager Michael Iwaniw said.
"The full effect of the Canadian situation is not yet known but it is expected that if their poor weather continues, all their remaining barley crops will be feed quality," he said.
With the tightening of supply, EU Commissioners should see reason and "back off the subsidy wagon" which would allow malting barley prices to improve, he said.
Iwaniw said Canada's weather would add to the world supply of feed grain, a commodity already abundant.
"Prospects for the United States corn crop have also continued to improve, with a resultant weakening in corn futures," he said.

Iwaniw said completely unnecessary European subsidies on feed barley over the last month had pushed prices down and these only stabilised a couple of weeks ago when Saudi Arabia put out a tender for 1.7 million tonnes.

"The European subsidies were ridiculous because their supply situation meant they were always going to get the majority of the Saudi tender, but the damage has been done now and the base at which prices stabilised was lower than our earlier pool estimate had allowed for...," he said.
The board markets barley from the states of South Australia and Victoria. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
